name: Collared Crow
rangeDescription: Central and eastern china to northern vietnam; hainan and taiwan
description: By far the most distinctive crow of farmland, fields, and other open spaces: adults black with white hindneck connecting to white breast band. Superficially similar to adult Daurian Jackdaw, but the latter is more compact and smaller, with pale plumage extending through the belly.

name: Ampay Tapaculo
rangeDescription: Andes of south-central peru (apurímac)
description: Dark gray tapaculo with a pale eyebrow known only from a few sites in the eastern Andes of southern Peru. While long known to be something different, it was finally described as a new species in 2020.

name: Kandt's Waxbill
rangeDescription: Rift valley mountains of far eastern democratic republic of the congo, uganda, burundi, rwanda, and kenya
description: Pretty waxbill that is gray, black, and white, with red highlights. The bright red rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Socorro Parakeet
rangeDescription: Socorro island (revillagigedo islands off western mexico)
description: Bright green bird with long, pointed tail. Bill is dull pink.

name: Luzon Rail
rangeDescription: Montane north-central luzon (northern philippines); few recent records
description: A mysterious medium-sized rail, possibly of foothill or montane grassy areas and forests. Dark brown above with a pale gray chest, a whitish throat, a barred belly, blackish legs, and a fairly long, curved reddish bill.

name: Taiwan Scimitar-Babbler
rangeDescription: Taiwan
description: Medium-sized, strikingly patterned songbird endemic to Taiwan, where fairly common. Brown above, white below, with white supercilium, black mask, and heavy black spots on the breast.

name: Acre Antshrike
rangeDescription: Western amazonian brazil in serra do divisor national park
description: Secretive, rare medium-sized antshrike of the dense forests of the Cordillera Divisor of remote western Brazil and eastern Peru. Males are dark gray with a bluish tint to the back and upperparts, while females are bluish-gray above and brownish-orange below.

name: Brown Parrotbill
rangeDescription: Bamboo forest of nepal to southeastern tibet, southwestern china, and northeastern myanmar
description: Dark brown parrotbill with a stout yellow bill and an arching black eyebrow. Like many other parrotbills, shows a strong affinity for high-elevation bamboo thickets, in which it moves about noisily in small flocks.

name: Bristle-thighed Curlew
rangeDescription: Breeds western alaska; winters hawaii and micronesia to polynesia
description: A large shorebird with a long, curved bill. Similar to Whimbrel but warmer brown and with a cinnamon-colored rump.

name: Southern Red-billed Hornbill
rangeDescription: Angola and northern namibia to mozambique and eastern south africa
description: A small, black-and-white hornbill with a petite red bill; male has a black base to the mandible. Pairs occur in open savanna with sparse ground cover, where they hop on the ground foraging for invertebrates.

name: White-whiskered Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: Extraordinarily plumaged songbird with white facial markings that lend it an almost comical whiskered appearance. Brown overall, with accents of yellow, buff, purple, plum, blue, and orange throughout the plumage.

name: Pohnpei Lorikeet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of pohnpei (eastern caroline islands)
description: Beautiful dark maroon parrot with a bright orange bill and yellowish tail. Found solely on the island of Pohnpei in the eastern Caroline Islands, where it is the only naturally-occurring parrot.

name: Mindanao Plumed-Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (mindanao)
description: A tiny and uncommon bird of foothill and lower montane forest on Mindanao. Yellowish to off-white below with a small eyebrow mainly in front of the eye, brown upperparts, and a grayish head.

name: Ovambo Sparrowhawk
rangeDescription: Locally in savanna and thornscrub of sub-saharan africa
description: Medium-sized sparrowhawk that is normally gray, but there is a rare black morph. In all plumages, shows diagnostic white streaks along the central part of the tail, but these are hard to see.

name: Chestnut-backed Laughingthrush
rangeDescription: Lowlands of northeastern india (arunachal pradesh) to northern myanmar
description: A myna-sized bird with a large white cheek patch and a black forehead, chin, and throat. Note the gray belly, the reddish back, and a small white patch on the forehead.

name: Oriental Magpie
rangeDescription: Southeastern russia, northeastern china, and korea southward through eastern china, taiwan, and hainan to northern myanmar, northern laos, and northern vietnam
description: Conspicuous black-and-white bird with a long tail; wings and tail shine with green and blue gloss in good lighting. A common inhabitant of open and semi-open habitats such as fields and farmlands, often seen perched up on power lines or fence posts.

name: Andaman Coucal
rangeDescription: Andaman islands and adjacent table, great and little coco islands
description: A large, pale-brown, ground-dwelling cuckoo with rusty wings and back. Skulks in bushes and low cover, where it moves clumsily as it searches for small invertebrates, small mammals, and birds to prey on.

name: Lesser Flamingo
rangeDescription: Locally from africa and madagascar to northwestern india
description: The smallest flamingo in the world, with a dark bill and red legs. Note glowing red eyes in adults.

name: Bare-eyed Antbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern amazonian brazil (rio tapajós to rio iriri, southward to mato grosso)
description: Fantastic-looking antbird with a bold whitish bare eye-ring and a restricted range. Males have a black head and breast, and are otherwise cinnamon-brown; females are duller around the head, but otherwise also cinnamon.

name: Taiwan Liocichla
rangeDescription: Montane forest of taiwan
description: The gloom of the forest may make this small songbird of dense montane forests and edges appear dark, but a bit of sunlight reveals a gloriously colorful plumage, with subtle patches of olive, blue, yellow, orange, and chestnut. Social, moving about in pairs or flocks, often emerging out into the open when gaps in the vegetation are present.
